research.headline: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
research.summary: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner.

As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law,….

research.headline: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
research.summary: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-11}$ or better.

research.headline: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
research.summary: Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) aligns a language model to a general preference function by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player preference game. Its practical variant, DNO-Prct, iterates on-policy sampling, LLM-based rating of the samples together with a teacher's gold response, large-margin preference-pair selection and a DPO-style contrastive update. We re-implement DNO-Prct independently and study it on two open-weight instruct models, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1, with GPT-4o or a larger open-weight model of the same family as the annotator.

frontier.headline: Interpretable Quantum Photonic Generative Models
frontier.summary: We propose a physical generative model for learning correlated multivariate data based on homodyne detection of photonic continuous-variable (CV) circuits. We use an $N$-mode photonic circuit in which two-mode squeezing provides correlations, local phase shifts tune the strength and sign of these correlations, and an adjustable interferometer redistributes them across modes. We train the circuit by matching its Pearson correlation matrix to the one obtained from data.

frontier.headline: Quantum Error Correction in Nearly Critical Toric Codes
frontier.summary: We investigate quantum error correction protocols for topological codes deformed away from their stabilizer limits, particularly as they are pushed towards quantum phase transitions into trivial phases. Our focus is primarily on quantum information stored within the ground-state manifold of the transverse-field toric code (TFTC), subjected to independent bit-flip and phase-flip decoherence. Although the transverse field induces strong quantum fluctuations of $m$ anyons in the ground states, we show that projective measurements of the "bare" toric code stabilizers can nevertheless be used to construct an efficient decoding algorithm which exhibits a finite threshold to both types of decoherence, even when the transverse field is tuned infinitesimally close to the quantum critical point.

frontier.headline: Universal dynamics of quantum phase transitions with fractional long-range interactions
frontier.summary: The complete statistical characterization of defects generated in a quantum phase transition has mostly been studied in exactly solvable models, and remains little explored in nonintegrable systems such as long-range interacting spin chains. We characterize the full defect counting statistics in a nonintegrable long-range spin chain, the fractional Ising model, by time-dependent variational-principle simulations within the matrix-product-state and matrix-product-operator formalism. Fractional interactions capture emergent multiscale correlations and long-range effects in nature, governed by the order of the underlying fractional derivative.

frontier.headline: Effective Hamiltonians and non-Hermitian physics
frontier.summary: Every realistic quantum system is coupled to an environment. Including the environment restores a closed, Hermitian description, but at the cost of an intractably large Hilbert space. The Feshbach--Löwdin projection eliminates the unwanted degrees of freedom exactly, yielding an effective Hamiltonian $H_{\rm eff}$ on the relevant subspace alone---which \new{generically becomes non-Hermitian when the eliminated subspace contains an energetically accessible continuum and outgoing boundary conditions are imposed}.

voices.headline: DOJ’s Try-Anything Approach
voices.summary: I n the run-up to the 2024 election, Donald Trump complained that Special Counsel Jack Smith’s detailed overview of the evidence against him in the January 6 case constituted “Election Interference.” The Department of Justice had a policy of not taking any potentially influential action so soon before an election, Trump rightly noted in a social-media post, and Smith, Trump argued more debatably, had just violated those rules. Trump seems a great deal less worried about DOJ’s propriety now. Over just the past few weeks, DOJ has sued multiple states challenging their election processes, charged more than 100 people with alleged voter fraud, and launched a barrage of criminal charges and investigations against Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar, former FBI Director James Comey, and other figures hated by MAGA.

voices.headline: Israel’s Common Ground
voices.summary: My most recent visit to Israel overlapped with its election in October, but that was a coincidence. In 10 days of discussions with generals and intelligence officers, entrepreneurs and university students, I was reminded of what Moshe Dayan’s biographer Shabtai Teveth wrote about Israel’s famous one-eyed soldier and diplomat: “His one eye glimmered with an enormous lust for life, his other eye was extinguished beneath the black patch, dead. At times he seemed to symbolize Israel itself, in which life and death are close partners.” I had visited Israel in November 2023, while the horrors of the Hamas onslaught were still fresh—more than 800 civilians and 300 soldiers killed, 251 hostages seized.

voices.headline: Haley Stevens Is Sending the Wrong Message
voices.summary: ET on November 1, 2026 Haley Stevens nearly won the Democratic nomination for Senate in Michigan in August, then immediately endorsed the winner, Abdul El-Sayed. She has spent the months since then vacillating, expressing doubts about his campaign while maintaining her support. But last week, her fiancé said that he intends to vote for El-Sayed’s opponent, Mike Rogers, and now she has followed, endorsing the Republican just two days before the election.
